questions.subtopic: Vetti and agrarian relations in pre-statehood Telangana
questions.stem: In the agrarian and social history of pre-statehood Telangana, the term 'vetti' most directly referred to which practice?
options: A land-revenue assessment paid in cash
A system of forced unpaid labour imposed on dependent households
A hereditary grant of tax-free land
explanations: Vetti was not simply a cash land-revenue assessment.
Correct. Vetti referred to forced, unpaid labour exacted from oppressed rural communities and was a major grievance in Telangana's agrarian history.
A voluntary grain bank is a community support mechanism, not forced labour.
A tax-free land grant is not the meaning of vetti.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state; SCERT Telangana, Class VIII Social Studies, Telangana Armed Struggle and vetti; https://www.scert.telangana.gov.in/pdf/publication/ebooks2019/8th%20social%20em.pdf

questions.subtopic: Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act: common capital provision
questions.stem: Under Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was provided as the common capital of the successor States for a period not exceeding how long from the appointed day?
explanations: Five years is shorter than the statutory maximum.
Correct. Section 5 provides for Hyderabad as common capital for a period not exceeding ten years from the appointed day.
Fifteen years is not the limit specified in Section 5.
The Act itself specifies a maximum period; it is not left wholly open-ended for later legislation.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Socio-economic, Political and Cultural History of Telangana with special emphasis on Telangana Statehood Movement and formation of Telangana state; Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Section 5; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/

questions.stem: Under Article 243-I of the Constitution, who constitutes the State Finance Commission and at what interval?
options: The President of India every five years
The Governor of the State every five years
The State Legislature every six years
The Election Commission of India every five years
explanations: The President constitutes the Union Finance Commission under Article 280, not the State Finance Commission under Article 243-I.
Correct. The Governor constitutes a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats.
The Constitution assigns constitution of the State Finance Commission to the Governor, not the State Legislature at a six-year interval.
The Election Commission of India has no role in constituting the State Finance Commission.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; Constitution of India, Article 243-I; https://legislative.gov.in/constitution-of-india/

questions.subtopic: State Election Commission and Panchayat elections
questions.stem: Which constitutional provision vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and conduct of, Panchayat elections in a State Election Commission?
explanations: Article 243-I concerns the State Finance Commission.
Correct. Article 243-K provides for the State Election Commission's control over Panchayat elections.
Article 280 establishes the Union Finance Commission.
Article 324 concerns the Election Commission of India and elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Indian Constitution; Indian Political System; Governance and Public Policy; Constitution of India, Article 243-K; https://legislative.gov.in/constitution-of-india/

questions.subtopic: POSH Act: constitution of Internal Committee
questions.stem: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, an employer is required to constitute an Internal Committee at a workplace having at least how many employees?
explanations: Five employees is below the statutory threshold.
Eight employees is also below the threshold.

Correct. Section 4 requires an Internal Committee at every workplace with ten or more employees; the Act provides for a Local Committee in specified cases where an Internal Committee is not constituted.
Twenty is not the threshold; the requirement begins at ten employees.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, Section 4; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/

questions.subtopic: Maternity Benefit Act: duration of paid maternity leave
questions.stem: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended in 2017, the ordinary paid maternity-benefit period for an eligible woman with fewer than two surviving children is:
explanations: Twelve weeks applies in specified cases such as a woman with two or more surviving children and certain adopting or commissioning mothers, not the ordinary category asked here.
Eighteen weeks is not the statutory period introduced by the 2017 amendment.
Twenty weeks is not the statutory period in Section 5(3).
Correct. The 2017 amendment increased the entitlement to 26 weeks for an eligible woman with fewer than two surviving children, with not more than eight weeks before the expected delivery date.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Social Exclusion; Rights issues such as Gender, Caste, Tribe, Disability etc. and inclusive policies; Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended by Act 6 of 2017, Section 5(3); India Code; https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/12874/1/the_maternity_benefit_act%2C_1961_no._53_of_1961_date_12.12.1961.pdf

questions.subtopic: Nagoba Jatara and Gond cultural traditions
questions.stem: Nagoba Jatara, a major Gond tribal festival in Telangana, is traditionally held at which place?
options: Keslapur in Indravelli mandal, Adilabad district
explanations: Correct. Telangana Tourism identifies Nagoba Jatara with Keslapur village in Indravelli mandal of Adilabad district; it is associated with the Mesaram clan of Gonds.
Medaram is associated with the Sammakka–Saralamma Jatara, a different tribal festival.
Basar is known for the Gnana Saraswati temple on the Godavari.
Alampur is known for its temple complex and is not the venue of Nagoba Jatara.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; SCERT Telangana, Class V EVS, Nagoba fair at Keslapur, Indravelli mandal, Adilabad district; https://scert.telangana.gov.in/pdf/publication/ebooks2019/5%20evs%20bilingual%20part%201%202022-23.pdf

questions.stem: Which manufacturing technique is characteristically associated with Telangana's traditional Dokra metal craft?
explanations: Wheel-thrown pottery is a ceramic process, not the characteristic Dokra metal-casting method.
Correct. Dokra is a traditional non-ferrous metal craft made through the lost-wax casting process.
Ikat-resist dyeing is a textile technique associated with woven patterns, not metal casting.
Repoussé is a sheet-metal relief technique and does not describe the characteristic lost-wax process.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; Telangana Tourism, Arts & Crafts – Dokra metal craft of Adilabad and lost-wax casting; https://www.tourism.telangana.gov.in/page/arts-crafts

questions.subtopic: Nirmal toys: material and regional identity
questions.stem: Nirmal's traditional wooden toys and related craft are associated with which Telangana district?
explanations: Adilabad is associated with several tribal crafts, but Nirmal toys are identified with Nirmal.
Correct. Nirmal district is the regional centre associated with Nirmal wooden toys and paintings.
Warangal is especially associated with Kakatiya heritage and other crafts, not the Nirmal toy tradition.
Sangareddy is not the district from which the Nirmal craft takes its name.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; Telangana Tourism, Nirmal destination – wooden Nirmal toys; https://tourism.telangana.gov.in/destinations/nirmal

questions.stem: Which description most accurately identifies Bathukamma as a Telangana cultural observance?
options: A harvest boat race conducted on the Godavari
A floral festival in which women arrange seasonal flowers in tiered formations and celebrate collectively
A martial dance performed exclusively by Kakatiya soldiers
A Buddhist monastic ceremony held at Phanigiri
explanations: Bathukamma is not a boat race.
Correct. Bathukamma is a floral festival centred on seasonal flowers, community singing and collective celebration by women.
The martial dance association is closer to Perini Sivatandavam, not Bathukamma.
Phanigiri is an archaeological Buddhist site; Bathukamma is not a monastic ceremony.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Society, Culture, Heritage, Arts and Literature of Telangana; Telangana Tourism, Warangal destination and Bathukamma festival; https://tourism.telangana.gov.in/destinations/warangal

questions.stem: Under the Mission Bhagiratha design described by the Telangana Government, what is the planned treated piped-water service level for rural households?
explanations: 55 LPCD is not the rural service norm in the Mission Bhagiratha description.
70 LPCD is not the stated rural target.
Correct. The State's Mission Bhagiratha material specifies 100 LPCD for rural areas, 135 LPCD for municipalities and 150 LPCD for municipal corporations.
150 LPCD is the stated norm for municipal corporations, not rural households.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; Telangana Drinking Water Supply Corporation, Mission Bhagiratha service levels (100 LPCD rural, 135 LPCD municipalities, 150 LPCD municipal corporations); https://mbbulk.telangana.gov.in/mbbulkweb/about.html

questions.stem: Which set of activities most directly reflects the physical restoration work undertaken under Mission Kakatiya?
options: Desilting tank beds, repairing sluices and weirs, strengthening bunds and restoring feeder channels
Deepening only major river channels and constructing coastal ports
Replacing all minor irrigation tanks with groundwater borewells
Lining every village road and installing rooftop solar panels
explanations: Correct. These are the core tank-restoration components identified by Telangana's irrigation administration.
Major river channels and ports are outside the programme's tank-restoration scope.
The programme restores minor irrigation tanks rather than replacing them with borewells.
Road construction and rooftop solar installation are not the defining Mission Kakatiya works.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; Government of Telangana, Mission Kakatiya – desilting, feeder-channel, bund, weir and sluice restoration; https://www.telangana.gov.in/mission-kakatiya/

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes Telangana's Rythu Bima from an agricultural crop-insurance scheme?
options: It compensates only for measured crop-yield loss after drought
It is a group life-insurance scheme that provides a death benefit to the enrolled farmer's nominee
It is a loan-waiver programme for all rural households
It reimburses the cost of irrigation electricity for tenant farmers
explanations: Crop-yield loss compensation is the role of crop-insurance arrangements, not Rythu Bima's core design.
Correct. Rythu Bima is a farmer group life-insurance scheme; the official portal describes a ₹5 lakh insured amount paid to the nominee on the enrolled farmer's death.
Rythu Bima is not a general household loan-waiver programme.
Electricity reimbursement is not the benefit described for Rythu Bima.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Policies of Telangana State; Jogulamba Gadwal District Government, Agriculture Schemes – Rs 5 lakh life-insurance cover for farmers under Rythu Bima; https://gadwal.telangana.gov.in/scheme-category/agricultural/

questions.stem: A treatment operator mixes 120 litres of water containing a dissolved tracer at 30 mg/L with 80 litres containing the same tracer at 10 mg/L. Assuming volumes are additive and no tracer is lost, what is the final concentration?
explanations: 18 mg/L would correspond to a different weighted total; the tracer mass is 3,600 + 800 = 4,400 mg.
20 mg/L is the unweighted mean of the two concentrations and ignores the unequal volumes.
Correct. Final concentration = (120×30 + 80×10)/(120+80) = 4,400/200 = 22 mg/L.
24 mg/L is not obtained from the conserved tracer mass divided by the total volume.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; weighted-average concentration calculation, based on conservation of solute mass.

questions.subtopic: Pipes and cisterns: two inlets and one outlet
questions.stem: In a test tank, inlet A fills the tank in 12 hours, inlet B fills it in 18 hours, and an outlet empties a full tank in 36 hours. If all three operate together from empty, how long will the tank take to fill?
explanations: Six hours would require a net rate of one-sixth tank per hour, greater than the actual net rate.
Eight hours is not consistent with the combined rates.
Correct. Net rate = 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/36 = 4/36 = 1/9 tank per hour, so the tank fills in 9 hours.
Twelve hours ignores the positive contribution of inlet B and the outlet's smaller emptying rate.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; work-rate and combined-efficiency problem.

questions.stem: A water utility reduces non-revenue water from 25% of system input to 20%, with input volume unchanged at 40 million litres per day. By what percentage has the volume of non-revenue water fallen relative to its original volume?
explanations: Five percentage points is the absolute reduction in the share, not the percentage fall relative to the original loss volume.
15% is not obtained by comparing 10 with the original 25.
Correct. Original loss is 0.25×40 = 10 MLD; new loss is 0.20×40 = 8 MLD. The reduction is 2/10 = 20%.
25% would be the reduction only if the loss fell from 10 to 7.5 MLD.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Logical Reasoning; Analytical Ability and Data Interpretation; percentage change and water-loss interpretation.

questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct completion: 'If the isolation valve ___ before the pump started, the tank ___ overflowed.'
options: had been closed; would not have
explanations: 'Was closed; will not have' mixes an unsuitable past condition with a future-perfect result.
Correct. The third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause ('had been closed') and 'would have' plus past participle in the result clause.
'Would be closed; had not' reverses the clause structure and does not form the required conditional.
'Has closed; would not' mixes present perfect with an incomplete conditional result.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Basic English (10th class Standard); standard English grammar reference, third conditional / unreal past condition.

questions.subtopic: English usage: discuss versus discuss about
questions.stem: Select the sentence that uses the verb 'discuss' correctly in standard formal English.
options: The engineers discussed about the leakage report.
The engineers discussed the leakage report during the meeting.
The engineers discussed on the leakage report during the meeting.
The engineers discussed regarding the leakage report.
explanations: 'Discuss about' is redundant in standard usage because 'discuss' takes a direct object.
Correct. 'Discussed the leakage report' uses the verb with its direct object.
'Discussed on' is not the standard transitive construction in this sentence.
'Discussed regarding' is also an incorrect or needlessly redundant construction here.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Basic English (10th class Standard); Oxford Learner's Dictionaries / standard transitive verb usage for 'discuss'; https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/

questions.stem: A random variable X has mean 20 and variance 9. Using Chebyshev's inequality, what is the largest guaranteed upper bound on P(|X−20| ≥ 6)?
explanations: 1/2 is a weaker bound than the inequality gives for this deviation.
1/3 is also larger than the Chebyshev bound.
Correct. Chebyshev gives P(|X−μ|≥a) ≤ σ²/a² = 9/36 = 1/4.
1/9 would require a deviation of three standard deviations, not two.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; Sheldon Ross, A First Course in Probability, Chebyshev inequality; https://www.pearson.com/

questions.subtopic: Sampling distribution of the sample mean
questions.stem: A population has variance 16. A simple random sample of 25 independent observations is drawn. What is the variance of the sample mean, assuming sampling with replacement or an effectively infinite population?
explanations: 16 is the population variance, not the variance of the mean of 25 independent observations.
4 is the population standard deviation, not the required variance.
Correct. Var(X̄)=σ²/n=16/25=0.64 under the stated independence assumption.
0.16 would incorrectly divide the variance by 100.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; Ross, A First Course in Probability, sampling distributions and variance of the sample mean.

questions.stem: The lifetime T of a component follows an exponential distribution with mean 5 hours. Given that it has already operated for 3 hours, what is the probability that it operates for at least 5 additional hours?
explanations: e⁻⁵ would correspond to a five-hour interval at rate 1 per hour, not rate 1/5 per hour.
Correct. The exponential distribution is memoryless: P(T>8 | T>3)=P(T>5)=e^(−5/5)=e⁻¹.
1−e⁻¹ is the probability of failure within the next five hours, not survival for at least five hours.
e⁻⁸⁄⁵ is the probability of surviving eight hours from the start, not five additional hours conditional on surviving three.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; Ross, A First Course in Probability, exponential distribution and memoryless property.

questions.stem: If the number of service interruptions in a fixed interval follows a Poisson distribution with parameter λ=2, what is the probability of observing no interruptions in that interval?
explanations: 2e⁻² is the probability of exactly one event, not zero.
Correct. For X~Poisson(2), P(X=0)=e⁻²·2⁰/0!=e⁻².
1−e⁻² is the probability of at least one event.
2e⁻¹ is not the Poisson probability mass at zero for λ=2.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Probability and Statistics; Ross, A First Course in Probability, Poisson distribution.

questions.stem: Let A contain 3 distinct elements and B contain 5 distinct elements. How many one-to-one functions f:A→B are possible?
explanations: 15 counts 3×5 only if assignments are not distinguished correctly across all domain elements.
30 omits one factor in the falling factorial count.
Correct. The images of the three distinct elements must be distinct: 5×4×3=60 injective functions.
125=5³ counts all functions, including those that map different elements of A to the same element of B.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, functions and one-to-one mappings.

questions.stem: A square matrix A satisfies A²=A. Which set contains every possible eigenvalue of A over the complex numbers?
explanations: An eigenvalue of −1 would require 1=−1 after applying A²=A to an eigenvector, which is impossible.
Correct. If Av=λv, then A²v=λ²v and Av=λv; hence λ²=λ, so λ(λ−1)=0 and λ is 0 or 1.
The equation restricts eigenvalues to two values, not arbitrary non-zero reals.
Roots of unity other than 1 do not generally satisfy λ²=λ.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, eigenvalues and idempotent linear operators.

questions.subtopic: Orthogonality of eigenvectors of symmetric matrices
questions.stem: For a real symmetric matrix, eigenvectors corresponding to two distinct eigenvalues are necessarily:
options: Orthogonal under the usual inner product
Equal in magnitude component by component
explanations: Eigenvectors associated with distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent, not dependent.
Correct. Real symmetric matrices are self-adjoint; eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.
There is no requirement that their components have equal magnitudes.
A real symmetric matrix may have non-zero eigenvalues; the statement concerns eigenvectors, not zero eigenvalues.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; standard spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices, e.g. Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right.
